title: In 1618 Protestant nobles threw three men out of a Prague Castle window. All survived

cover.alt: Two men in black doublets tumble down the stone wall of a castle from a high window towards a heap of papers below.

body: On 23 May 1618 Protestant nobles, angry at what they saw as Catholic attacks on their religious freedoms, burst into the Bohemian Chancellery in Prague Castle and threw two of the king's regents, **Jaroslav Bořita of Martinic** and **Vilém Slavata**, out of a window, followed by their secretary **Philipp Fabricius**. Slavata later put the fall at over 28 Prague ells, about 16.5 metres. All three survived, though Slavata cut his head, and shots were fired at them as they got away. Catholics said the Virgin Mary had held Martinic up on her cloak; Protestants said the men had landed on a heap of paper. The famous dung heap seems to be a later story. Fabricius was ennobled as 'von Hohenfall', 'of the high fall'. The defenestration set off a Bohemian revolt that grew into the Thirty Years' War.

slides.alt: A room in Prague Castle. Two angry Protestant nobles in wide black hats and ruffs point accusingly at two alarmed Catholic regents in black by a tall window.
slides.caption: Prague Castle, 23 May 1618. Protestant nobles, furious with the Catholic regents, have come to talk. Briefly.

bubbles.text: Gentlemen, surely we can discuss this—
bubbles.speaker: A regent

slides.alt: The tall stone wall of the castle. From a high window a noble points down as three men in black tumble through the air, arms flailing.
slides.caption: Out go two regents and their secretary: a drop of about 16 metres.

bubbles.text: We'll see if his Mary helps him.
bubbles.speaker: Oldřich Kinsky

slides.alt: At the foot of the wall the three dazed men sit in a heap of papers, stars round one head. Beside them hovers a woman in a wide blue cloak with a halo.
slides.caption: All three survive. Catholics thank the Virgin Mary and her cloak, Protestants a heap of paper. The dung heap is a later legend.

bubbles.text: I expect a title for this.
bubbles.speaker: Philipp Fabricius

slides.question: What did Fabricius's new noble name mean?
slides.explanation: In 1623 he became Fabricius 'von Hohenfall', 'of the high fall', for the fall he survived.

source.label: Peter Wilson, 'The Thirty Years War' (Gresham College lecture, 2018)
